questions.q: How do most Oracle Fusion Expenses policy limits behave when an employee enters an amount over the limit?
options: The system usually flags it as a soft violation requiring justification and audit review, rather than blocking submission
The expense report is permanently deleted
The employee's manager is automatically fired
Nothing happens at all; policy limits are purely cosmetic
questions.explain: Most policy limits are soft limits: the item can still be submitted, but it is flagged, requires justification, and is routed for audit review.

questions.q: When is a true hard limit (one that blocks submission entirely) typically used?
options: For every single expense type without exception
Only for airfare
Only for a small number of expense types where leadership decided no justification should be possible
Hard limits do not exist in Oracle Fusion Expenses
questions.explain: Hard limits are reserved for cases like a strict company-wide prohibition, such as no personal mileage reimbursement on a company car.

questions.q: Which of the following can cause the SAME expense type to have different dollar limits for different people?
options: The day of the week the report is submitted
The color of the receipt
The employee's home internet provider
Employee grade/role and geography
questions.explain: Policies commonly vary by grade or role (director vs. technician) and by geography (per diem rates differ by destination).

questions.q: Besides the dollar ceiling, what else is considered part of an expense type's 'policy' in Oracle Fusion Expenses?
options: Receipt requirements and justification requirements
The employee's home address
The company's stock price
The weather at the time of the expense
questions.explain: Policy also governs whether a receipt is required, whether itemization is required, and whether a justification comment must be entered.

questions.q: In the Marcus Webb client dinner example, what happened after he entered a $410 meal against a $300 policy limit?
options: The expense report was immediately and permanently rejected with no option to proceed
He was required to enter a justification, and the item still submitted but was flagged for mandatory audit review
The system automatically lowered the amount to $300
Nothing was flagged since meals are never subject to policy
questions.explain: The overage triggered a required justification and a mandatory audit flag, but did not block Marcus from submitting the report.
